process_area.title: Third-Party Inventory, Tiering & Cross-Domain Risk Framework

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager / Third-Party Risk Lead
fields.Participants: Procurement (VS-03/VS-34), Vendor Mgmt (VS-03), IT (VS-27), Finance (VS-17), Compliance (VS-22), business owners
fields.Trigger: New third-party onboarding; periodic inventory reconcile; TPRM setup
fields.Volume: 1 enterprise register; ~800–1,000 merchandise vendors + ~hundreds of non-merchandise/SaaS/3PL/payment/BPO/CIT/professional third parties

Automation Opportunity: - Register auto-populated from procurement/AP/IT/contracts; shadow-third-party detection from AP spend
Controls: - CTL-713 (ensure controlled execution — Third-Party Inventory, Tiering & Cross-Domain Risk Framework (PA-161.1).)
- CTL-713: single enterprise register; reconciled quarterly to AP/procurement/IT; feeds all risk-domain slices
Cross-references: - links to VS-03/VS-34 (procurement), VS-15 (AP), VS-99 (IT asset), VS-100.3 (contracts), W4723 (tiering); consolidates W1328/W334/W2942/W3052/W3863/W3733 scope
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-third-party risk**: A SaaS/BPO/provider transacting without a register entry → unmanaged risk; mitigated by the AP/procurement reconcile that surfaces unregistered spend
- **Fragmented-inventory risk**: Each function keeping its own vendor list → no enterprise view; mitigated by the single register
System Touchpoints: - TPRM platform/register; procurement/vendor (VS-03/VS-34); AP (VS-15); IT/SaaS (VS-99); contracts (VS-100.3); records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain the enterprise third-party inventory & relationship register: every external party with type (merchandise vendor, 3PL, SaaS/cloud, payment, BPO, CIT, security agency, sourcing agent, marketplace seller, professional/EPC), owning business/function, contract, spend, criticality tier (W4723), data-access posture (W4726), fourth-party exposure (W4724), and risk-domain scores

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Reconcile the register to procurement (VS-03/VS-34), AP (VS-15), IT/SaaS (VS-99), and contracts (VS-100.3) quarterly; flag third parties transacting without a register entry ("shadow third parties")

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Govern the register as the single source feeding each risk-domain slice (ABC VS-86.3, privacy VS-91.2, fraud VS-125.1, integrity VS-119.3, supply VS-21.2 W1328, audit VS-21.1 W334)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
fields.Participants: Head of Internal Audit & Risk (VS-21.2), Compliance (VS-22), Cyber (VS-27.3), Privacy (VS-91), Legal (VS-100.3), Procurement (VS-03)
fields.Trigger: TPRM setup; annual framework review; ERM refresh (VS-21.2)

workflows.name: TPRM Framework, Risk Taxonomy & Cross-Domain Risk Appetite

Automation Opportunity: - Cross-domain scoring model; appetite-linked tiering; domain-owner workflow integration
Controls: - CTL-713: cross-domain taxonomy ERM-aligned; domain-owners mapped; framework leadership-endorsed
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-86/VS-91/VS-125/VS-131/VS-27.3 (domain owners), W4723 (tiering)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Domain-silo risk**: Each domain scoring in isolation → no cross-domain view of a single third party; mitigated by the cross-domain taxonomy and shared register
- **Appetite-misalignment risk**: TPRM appetite not aligned to ERM → inconsistent decisions; mitigated by ERM alignment (VS-21.2)
System Touchpoints: - ERM/risk taxonomy (VS-21.2); TPRM platform; domain-owner systems (VS-86/VS-91/VS-125/VS-131/VS-27.3)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CEO
steps.activity: Define the TPRM framework and risk taxonomy: risk domains (financial, cyber/infosec, operational/resilience, regulatory/compliance, data-privacy, ESG/human-rights, geographic/geopolitical, concentration, fourth-party), inherent/residual scoring methodology, and risk-appetite per domain aligned to ERM (VS-21.2)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Map each risk domain to its domain-owner workflow (ABC VS-86.3, privacy VS-91.2, fraud VS-125.1, integrity VS-119.3, human-rights VS-131, supply VS-21.2, cyber VS-27.3, financial VS-105/VS-68); define how the TPRM backbone feeds and is fed by each

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CEO
steps.activity: Obtain leadership endorsement (Head of Internal Audit & Risk/CEO) and align to international standards (ISO 31000, NIST CSF supply-chain, SOC 2); publish the framework and train business/procurement owners
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

fields.Participants: Business/function owners, domain owners, Head of Internal Audit & Risk (VS-21.2)
fields.Trigger: New third party; annual re-tier; material change

workflows.name: Third-Party Tiering & Criticality Methodology (Inherent/Residual, All Domains)

Automation Opportunity: - Multi-factor scoring engine; material-change detection (data-access/spend/news); tier-driven DD/monitoring automation
Controls: - CTL-713 (ensure controlled execution — Third-Party Inventory, Tiering & Cross-Domain Risk Framework (PA-161.1).)
- CTL-713: inherent/residual scoring documented; re-tier on material change + annual; extends W1328 enterprise-wide
Cross-references: - extends VS-21.2 W1328 (supply-side tiering); links to W4721 (register), W4722 (taxonomy), W4724/W4726 (inputs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-tiering risk**: A critical third party tiered low → insufficient DD/monitoring → undetected risk; mitigated by the multi-factor inherent scoring
- **Static-tiering risk**: A tier not updated after a material change → stale risk view; mitigated by the material-change trigger and annual re-tier
System Touchpoints: - TPRM platform (scoring/tiering); ERM (VS-21.2); register (W4721); domain-owner systems
Time Estimate: - ~per third party 0.5–1 day initial; ~annual re-tier absorbed

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Tier each third party by inherent risk across all domains (W4722): spend/materiality, criticality to operations (sole/single-source, revenue-impact), data-access (W4726), fourth-party exposure (W4724), and domain-specific exposure; assign Criticality Tier (Critical/High/Medium/Low) driving the DD depth (PA-161.2) and monitoring cadence

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Compute residual risk after controls/DD (PA-161.2); escalate high-residual third parties; this extends enterprise-wide the supply-side tiering in VS-21.2 W1328 (which is scoped to merchandise-supply criticality)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain tiering transparency: document the scoring inputs and rationale; re-tier on material change (new data-access, acquisition, performance/financial deterioration); feed tiering to W1328 and each domain slice

fields.Participants: Privacy (VS-91), Cyber (VS-27.3), Procurement (VS-03), Legal (VS-100.3), third parties
fields.Trigger: New third party with sub-contracting; annual mapping; data-processor flow
fields.Volume: ~150–300 mapped fourth parties (SaaS sub-processors, 3PL sub-carriers, BPO sub-vendors)

Automation Opportunity: - Fourth-party disclosure/mapping platform; flow-down clause library; sub-processor-change alerts (VS-91.2)
Controls: - CTL-713: fourth parties disclosed and mapped; flow-down obligations in contracts; unacceptable exposure managed
Cross-references: - links to VS-91.2 W3052 (data-processor/sub-processor), VS-100.3 (contracts), W4725 (concentration), W4739 (resilience)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-fourth-party risk**: A SaaS vendor's cloud sub-processor unknown to BuildRight → unmanaged privacy/security risk; mitigated by disclosure requirements and mapping
- **Hidden-concentration risk**: A single fourth party serving many BuildRight third parties → systemic concentration (W4725); mitigated by fourth-party mapping
System Touchpoints: - TPRM platform (fourth-party mapping); privacy (VS-91.2 W3052); contracts (VS-100.3); cyber (VS-27.3)
Time Estimate: - ~per Critical/High third party 1–2 days mapping; ~annual refresh

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Identify fourth parties (sub-processors, sub-contractors) for each Critical/High third party — especially data-processing fourth parties (SaaS cloud/hosting sub-processors per VS-91) and logistics sub-carriers (VS-06/VS-56); require disclosure in contracts

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Map fourth-party exposure: which BuildRight data/processes touch which fourth party; assess concentration (a fourth party serving many BuildRight third parties = hidden concentration W4725) and flow-down obligations (privacy VS-91, security, ABC)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / VP Legal
steps.activity: Require flow-down of DD/controls/audit rights to fourth parties in contracts; monitor fourth-party changes (a third party adding a sub-processor per VS-91.2 W3052); manage unacceptable fourth-party exposure (W4739/W4740)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
fields.Participants: Supply Planning (VS-02), Procurement (VS-03), Treasury (VS-18), Cyber (VS-27.3), Sourcing (VS-122)
fields.Trigger: Annual analysis; new significant third party; geopolitical event
fields.Volume: 1 concentration view across all third-party types and geographies

workflows.name: Concentration, Single-Source & Geographic Risk Exposure Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Concentration analytics across register/fourth-party/geography; limit-breach alerts; KRI dashboards
Controls: - CTL-713: concentration analyzed annually + on event; limits per appetite; breaches mitigated (W4737); extends W1328
Cross-references: - extends VS-21.2 W1328 (supply concentration); links to VS-02.3 (supply risk), W4724 (fourth party), W4737 (mitigation), W4743 (KRIs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-concentration risk**: Concentration obscured by entity/contract structure (e.g., two "different" vendors owned by one parent, or shared fourth party); mitigated by the unified concentration view
- **Concentration-limit-breach risk**: Concentration exceeding appetite unaddressed; mitigated by limits and mitigation routing (W4737)
System Touchpoints: - TPRM platform (concentration analytics); supply (VS-02.3 W558/W763); treasury (VS-18); cyber (VS-27.3); ERM KRIs (VS-21.2)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Analyze concentration across all third-party types: sole/single-source vendors (cement, steel, cable), single 3PL/payment/SaaS/cloud providers, geographic concentration (single port/region/country of origin — VS-02.2/VS-110), and fourth-party concentration (W4724)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Supply / Procurement / Cyber

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Quantify concentration exposure (revenue/COGS/operations at risk from a single point of failure); set concentration limits per risk-appetite (W4722); extend the supply-side concentration view in VS-21.2 W1328 to all third-party types
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Drive mitigation for excessive concentration (dual-source/multi-vendor W4737, alternate qualification, geographic diversification); monitor concentration as a KRI (W4743) and report to the board (W4728)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with Privacy VS-91)
fields.Participants: Privacy (VS-91), Cyber (VS-27.3), Data Governance (VS-28), Legal (VS-100.3), business owners
fields.Trigger: New third party; data-access change; privacy review (VS-91)
fields.Volume: ~ all third parties with data access (SaaS, BPO, payment, marketplace, fraud/CDP providers)

workflows.name: Third-Party Data Classification & Data-Access/Processing Risk Scoping

Automation Opportunity: - Data-access inventory/scoping tool; DPA/scope-change monitoring; sensitivity-driven DD depth
Controls: - CTL-713: data-access scoped and classified; DPA/transfer mechanism per VS-91; changes monitored; exit data-return (W4740)
Cross-references: - links to VS-91/VS-91.2 (privacy/DPIA), VS-27.3 (cyber), VS-28 (data governance), W4730/W4731 (DD), W4740 (exit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Undocumented-data-access risk**: A third party accessing data BuildRight didn't know about/scope → privacy breach (VS-91); mitigated by data-access scoping and monitoring
- **Scope-creep risk**: A third party expanding data use beyond the DPA; mitigated by change-monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/DPIA (VS-91.2); cyber (VS-27.3); data governance (VS-28); contracts (VS-100.3); TPRM platform

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO
steps.activity: For each third party, scope data-access: what BuildRight/customer/employee data the third party (and fourth parties W4724) can access/process (PII VS-91, payment data PCI, credentials, IP); classify the data sensitivity

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO / CIO
steps.activity: Determine the data-protection posture required (DPA, transfer mechanism for cross-border, encryption, access controls, retention/disposal) per VS-91; scope privacy DD (W4731) and cyber DD (W4730) accordingly
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Privacy / Cyber / Legal

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO
steps.activity: Monitor data-access changes (scope creep, new data type, sub-processor W4724); manage unauthorized data-access/use; ensure data-return/deletion on exit (W4740)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with Treasury VS-18/VS-105 and ESG VS-25/VS-131)
fields.Participants: Treasury (VS-18), SCF (VS-105), ESG (VS-25), Human-Rights DD (VS-131), Procurement (VS-03)
fields.Trigger: New third party; annual screening; material event

workflows.name: Third-Party Financial, Solvency & ESG/Human-Rights Risk Screening

Automation Opportunity: - Financial/credit-screening feed; ESG/sanctions/Watch-list screening; findings-to-tiering integration
Controls: - CTL-713: Critical/High third parties financially screened annually; ESG/human-rights screened; findings feed tiering
Cross-references: - links to VS-18/VS-105 (financial/SCF), VS-25/VS-131 (ESG/human-rights), VS-122/VS-41 (import/PL exposure), W4723 (tiering)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sudden-failure risk**: A Critical vendor collapsing financially without warning → supply disruption; mitigated by financial screening and resilience (W4738)
- **Reputational/ESG risk**: A vendor with severe human-rights/environmental exposure damaging BuildRight's reputation/ESG posture; mitigated by ESG/human-rights DD (VS-131)
System Touchpoints: - Financial screening (Treasury VS-18/SCF VS-105); ESG/human-rights (VS-25/VS-131); procurement (VS-03); TPRM platform

steps.a: TPRM Lead / CFO
steps.activity: Screen third-party financial/solvency risk (credit, financials, going-concern indicators) for Critical/High third parties — especially sole-source and large-spend vendors; coordinate with Treasury (VS-18) and SCF (VS-105)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Screen ESG/human-rights risk (sanctions, modern-slavery, environmental, governance) per VS-131 and VS-25; especially for high-exposure geographies/categories (imports VS-122, private-label VS-41)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / ESG / Human-Rights DD

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Feed financial/ESG findings into the tiering (W4723) and the domain slices (VS-105 financial, VS-131 human-rights); manage unacceptable financial/ESG exposure (W4739/W4740)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
fields.Participants: Head of Internal Audit & Risk (VS-21.2), Compliance (VS-22), business/function owners, Board Risk Committee (VS-36)
fields.Trigger: Governance review; board cycle (VS-36); significant event

workflows.name: TPRM Governance, Ownership Matrix & Board Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Ownership-matrix workflow; board-report auto-roll; significant-event escalation
Controls: - CTL-713: every third party has a business + risk-domain owner; board reported quarterly; significant events escalated (VS-21.2)
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2/VS-36 (ERM/board), VS-21 (audit), VS-159 W4694 (incident escalation), W4743 (KRIs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ownership-vacuum risk**: A third party with no clear business/risk owner → unmanaged; mitigated by the ownership matrix
- **Board-blindness risk**: Board unaware of significant third-party exposure → governance failure; mitigated by quarterly reporting
System Touchpoints: - ERM/board reporting (VS-21.2/VS-36); TPRM platform; audit (VS-21); incident/crisis (VS-159 W4694)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain the TPRM governance & ownership matrix: each third party has a business owner (the function that uses it) and a risk-domain owner (privacy/cyber/ABC/etc.); the TPRM Program owns the backbone; define escalation paths
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Board
steps.activity: Report TPRM to the board risk committee (VS-36) quarterly: third-party inventory summary, Critical/High exposure, concentration (W4725), significant findings (PA-161.2), resilience posture (PA-161.3); integrate into ERM reporting (VS-21.2)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Board
steps.activity: Manage significant TPRM events (Critical third-party failure, breach, concentration shock) with executive/board notification per the ERM escalation (VS-21.2/W4694); assure via Internal Audit (VS-21)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Internal Audit
